title: Namibia — Dunes, Skeleton Coast & Etosha
sub: Seven days door to door — fly in from Joburg, five days from the red dunes to the great waterhole, and fly home. Tap a day to fly or drive it.
cap: Illustrative 5-day self-drive · real Namibian towns shown for bearing; lodges & food generic (SO-1b). A demo a real tour operator could publish as their own — free to claim and replace with their product. AI imagery. Flight fares are indicative cached data (Aviasales, 10 Aug 2026) — flights booked by your travel agency, never through MarketSquare.

days.title: Fly in from Joburg
days.summary: Two hours over the Kalahari — indicative return JNB ⇄ WDH from ~R5,200 (direct, cached 10 Aug 2026); your travel agency confirms and books it. Check live fares ↗ (indicative — your agency confirms & books)

stops.name: O.R. Tambo · departure
stops.blurb:
Boarding for the desert — the highveld falling away, the Kalahari turning apricot below.
Check live fares ↗ your agency confirms & books

stops.name: The Kalahari from above
stops.blurb: Red dune-streets in parallel lines to the horizon, a single farm light every hundred kilometres.

stops.name: Hosea Kutako · pick up the 4x4
stops.blurb:
Heat shimmer on the apron, keys to a kitted twin-cab, two spare wheels and a fridge in the back.
Check live fares ↗ your agency confirms & books

stops.name: Windhoek · first night
stops.blurb: Jacaranda streets and a first braai under a highland sky — the gravel starts tomorrow.

days.title: Into the red dunes
days.summary: South-west out of the capital, gravel roads unspooling into the oldest desert on earth.

stops.name: Windhoek · departure
stops.blurb: Highland capital, jacaranda streets, a last flat white before the gravel begins.

stops.name: Roadside grill stop
stops.blurb: Flame-grilled beef cut straight onto brown paper with a fist of coarse salt and chilli — the country's favourite roadside lunch.

stops.name: Dune country, first light
stops.blurb: Rust-red dunes 300 m tall, knife-edge crests, a dead white pan cracked like old porcelain.

stops.name: Desert camp under the escarpment
stops.blurb: Canvas and stone tucked below a rock wall; no light for 200 km, so the Milky Way does the ceiling.

days.title: Desert to the cold Atlantic
days.summary: Down the canyon road, across the gravel plains, into a coastal fog that never quite burns off.

stops.name: Dawn on the dunes
stops.blurb: Climb the high crest before sunrise; the sand goes from grey to blood-orange in four minutes.

stops.name: Canyon & gravel plains
stops.blurb: A deep rock gorge, then 200 km of pale gravel where the horizon shimmers and nothing moves.

stops.name: Lagoon oysters & flamingos
stops.blurb: Cold Atlantic oysters shucked at a lagoon shack, thousands of flamingos standing pink in the shallows.

stops.name: Seaside colonial town
stops.blurb: Pastel German colonial facades, palm-lined promenade, sea fog rolling in at four o'clock.

days.title: The Skeleton Coast
days.summary: North on the salt road where the desert runs straight into a cold, wrecking sea.

stops.name: Out on the salt road
stops.blurb: A road made of salt and gypsum, sea on the left, dunes on the right, fog between.

stops.name: Coastal bakery stop
stops.blurb: Apple strudel and strong coffee in a fishing village — a century-old German baking habit that never left.

stops.name: Cape fur seal colony
stops.blurb: A hundred thousand seals on one headland: the noise, the smell and the sheer churn of it.

stops.name: Shipwreck on the strand
stops.blurb: A rusting hull half-swallowed by sand, the reason this coast earned its name.

stops.name: Desert camp behind the dunes
stops.blurb: Wind-scoured camp behind the first dune line; jackal tracks past the tent by morning.

days.title: Damaraland & the desert elephants
days.summary: Inland into burnt-orange rock country, tracking elephants that walk on sand.

stops.name: Turning inland
stops.blurb: The fog lifts within twenty minutes and the temperature climbs twenty degrees.

stops.name: Ancient rock engravings
stops.blurb: Thousands of animals chipped into red sandstone by hunters six thousand years ago.

stops.name: Desert-adapted elephants
stops.blurb: A breeding herd moving down a dry riverbed, broad feet spread for sand, sixty kilometres between drinks.

stops.name: Three-legged pot supper
stops.blurb: Lamb, root vegetables and red wine left to collapse for five hours in a cast-iron pot over coals.

stops.name: Camp among the boulders
stops.blurb: Rooms built into a jumble of granite boulders, each one facing its own slice of valley.

days.title: The great white pan
days.summary: North to a salt pan so large it is visible from orbit, and the waterhole that draws everything to it.

stops.name: North to the park gate
stops.blurb: Mopane scrub thickens, the road reddens, and the first giraffe appears at the fence line.

stops.name: The salt pan edge
stops.blurb: A white nothing to the horizon, heat-shimmer turning distant zebra into floating smudges.

stops.name: Floodlit waterhole
stops.blurb: Elephant, rhino and lion take turns at the same water through the night; you just sit still and let it come.

stops.name: Braai under the thorn trees
stops.blurb: Game fillet and boerewors over hardwood coals, dust settling, the pan glowing pink behind.

stops.name: Journey's end · the waterhole
stops.blurb: Last night: a chair, a cold beer, and whatever chooses to walk out of the dark.

days.title: Drive south, fly home
days.summary: The long gravel south to Hosea Kutako, drop the keys, and the evening flight back to Joburg. Check live fares ↗ (indicative — your agency confirms & books)

stops.name: The long road south
stops.blurb: Four hundred kilometres of straight gravel and mirage — one last kudu crossing at dusk speed.

stops.name: Hosea Kutako · drop the keys
stops.blurb:
Dust off the twin-cab, one last biltong stop in the terminal, boarding for Johannesburg.
Check live fares ↗ your agency confirms & books

stops.name: Johannesburg · home
stops.blurb:
Red dust in the tread and ten thousand photos of dunes — tot siens, Namibia.
Check live fares ↗ your agency confirms & books

heritage: The world's only coastal fog desert — 300 m star dunes on the oldest desert on earth.
Thousands of animals chipped into red sandstone six thousand years ago.
A hundred thousand Cape fur seals on one headland.
The great white pan — waterholes that draw everything to them.
